business_problem: Airbus needs faster, easier access to complex technical and manufacturing documentation across engineering, manufacturing, after-sales service, and other operations while meeting the aerospace sector's regulatory and safety constraints.
solution_summary: Airbus is rolling out an internal generative AI programme to make technical knowledge easier to use across the company. A company-wide working group launched in 2023 to bring generative AI, large language models, and base models into Airbus under defined policies and safeguards. One concrete deployment is an AI assistant for Standard Operating Instructions, the manufacturing instructions used to build aircraft. The assistant works as a chatbot that lets factory staff query technical data in natural language instead of manually paging through documents on a tablet. Airbus is also running an after-sales service experiment to help support teams answer questions faster. In this implementation, internal document collections and technical instructions are the source material, large language models perform question understanding and answer generation, and chatbot-style interfaces serve the results back to employees in production and support workflows.

data_flow: Airbus feeds manufacturing instructions and other technical documentation into internal GenAI workflows, where large language models and base models interpret natural-language questions. The chatbot-based assistant returns targeted answers, such as the correct tool or procedure, to manufacturing staff and other employees through operational interfaces such as tablets.
